content.title: About
content.content: Fat‑free chocolate milk is a beverage made from skimmed cow’s milk (usually less than 0.5 % fat) to which cocoa powder, sugar and flavorings are added. It retains most of the nutrients of regular milk while offering a low‑calorie, smooth chocolate taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Skim milk provides almost the same amount of calcium as whole milk but with roughly half the calories.
The chocolate flavor is achieved by combining cocoa powder with a modest amount of sugar, making it popular among both children and calorie‑conscious adults.
In the United States, fat‑free chocolate milk is often marketed as a post‑workout recovery drink.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth and also supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: Skim milk provides about 3.4 g of protein per 100 ml, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa powder is high in flavonoids, which may reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience digestive discomfort after consuming dairy products.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Despite being low‑calorie, the drink contains added sugar, which may be a concern for diabetics or those limiting sugar intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey protein requires complete avoidance of dairy.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Enjoy chilled as a refreshing drink, blend into smoothies, use in protein shakes, or pour over oatmeal for a chocolate twist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Avoid freezing, as it can alter the texture.
